subject.title: Feature Request: Agent-triggered context compaction (self-compact tool)

question: Should OpenClaw expose a current-session-only model-callable self-compaction action through `session_status`, or keep compaction behind sender/control-plane boundaries until a different policy gate exists?
rationale: The missing API is clear, but the remaining choice is a product/security boundary: whether a model tool call may intentionally mutate active session context state without an authorized sender command.

options.title: Approve Narrow Self-Compaction
options.body: Allow a current-session-only `session_status` compact action after the linked PR is rebased and refreshed security/runtime proof is available.

options.title: Require Explicit Policy Gate
options.body: Keep the implementation direction but require an operator or tool-policy gate before exposing model-originated compaction.

options.title: Defer To Continuation Design
options.body: Do not land the narrow action until maintainers choose whether broader continuation APIs should own voluntary compaction.

recommendation.title: Approve Narrow Self-Compaction
recommendation.body: Allow a current-session-only `session_status` compact action after the linked PR is rebased and refreshed security/runtime proof is available.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest combined history across `session_status`, gateway/session surfaces, and compaction-adjacent runtime work.
